content:
- Overestimate prices in the short term after positive sentiment spikes; model tends to overshoot early in the 30-day horizon.
- Underestimate prices when sentiment is neutral or slightly negative; model reacts too slowly to downward sentiment signals.
- Exhibit mean reversion bias: forecasts often linger near recent highs, failing to adjust downward when sentiment turns negative.
- Lag in response to sentiment shifts: model delays correction after sentiment drops, leading to persistent overestimation.
- Overshoot after sharp sentiment upturns: model forecasts peak too high after positive sentiment, then fails to account for subsequent pullback.
- Horizon-specific error: 30-day forecasts consistently overpredict early days (1–7) when sentiment is positive, then underpredict later days (15–30) when sentiment turns negative.
- Sentiment-weighted adjustment: reduce forecast by 5–15% when sentiment is below 0.3, and increase by 5–10% when sentiment exceeds 0.7, especially in the first 10 days of the forecast horizon.
